findings.cross_file_justification: The loader admits insecure endpoints for every HTTP provider, but only OpenAIAdapter is changed to supply the TransportPolicy required by the shared transport.
findings.description: Non-OpenAI HTTP providers can now configure an opted-in private HTTP endpoint while continuing to call http_post without a policy. The default branch still honors proxy environment variables, and its urllib fallback still follows redirects. Consequently, an admitted provider does not receive the promised proxy and redirect protections.
findings.failure_mode: An Anthropic-type provider configured with an opted-in RFC1918 HTTP endpoint can send prompts and credentials through an environment-configured proxy; the urllib fallback can also follow a redirect outside the declared endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the provider transport policy to every HTTP adapter, or reject insecure-endpoint opt-ins for adapter types that do not enforce it.

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.hop_is_local / _local_labels / validate_local_fallbacks (full file) define a hop as local when the model entry OR, when the entry is silent, the provider block says dispatch_group: local. The planner (hop-locality.py) and the loader therefore admit a provider-block-level `dispatch_group: local` under locality local_voices. cheval's _build_provider_config only reads model_data.get("dispatch_group"), so ModelConfig.dispatch_group is None for every model of such a provider.
findings.description: ModelConfig.dispatch_group is populated from the model entry only. A provider that declares `dispatch_group: local` at the block level (accepted by validate_providers via _local_labels, and treated as local by hop_is_local / the planner) produces ModelConfig.dispatch_group=None. OpenAIAdapter._transport_policy then returns None unless allow_insecure_endpoint is also set, so an https endpoint on a loopback/RFC1918 host (which validate_providers admits without an opt-in) runs on the default transport: proxy environment variables (HTTPS_PROXY) are honoured and, on the urllib fallback, redirects are followed. The same gap makes modelinv.hop_locality_of record `hop_locality: hosted` for a hop the planner dispatched as local.
findings.failure_mode: Under hounfour.locality: local_voices, a prompt destined for a block-level-local provider is sent through whatever proxy the environment names (and may follow a redirect off-host on urllib), defeating the D-7.2 request-time guarantee; the MODELINV row simultaneously claims hop_locality=hosted, so the audit trail does not show the hop as local.
findings.suggested_fix: In _build_provider_config, fall back to the provider block: `dispatch_group=model_data.get("dispatch_group") or prov.get("dispatch_group")`. Better, derive the policy decision from the single rule: have cheval/_transport_policy call endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(hounfour, provider, model_id) (or carry its result into ModelConfig) instead of re-reading dispatch_group, and have modelinv.hop_locality_of delegate to the same function.

findings.description: validate_providers admits `allow_insecure_endpoint` and `dispatch_group: local` for every non-CLI provider type in the merged view, but the request-time half (TransportPolicy: trust_env=False, redirect refusal, path-prefix check) is wired only into OpenAIAdapter (complete/_dispatch/health_check). A provider of another HTTP type (e.g. type: anthropic) with an opted-in `http://10.x` endpoint passes load and then runs on the unchanged transport in its adapter.
findings.failure_mode: An opted-in http endpoint on a non-OpenAI-type provider is admitted at load but is sent in the clear through an environment proxy and, on urllib, follows redirects, contradicting the module docstring's statement that the adapter applies the request-time rules for every opted-in provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Either refuse `allow_insecure_endpoint` / `dispatch_group: local` at load for provider types whose adapter does not implement TransportPolicy, or plumb `policy=` into the other adapters' http_post/http_post_stream calls the same way OpenAIAdapter does.

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.hop_is_local is documented as the ONE implementation for cheval's planner, the loader and MODELINV hop_locality, but modelinv.hop_locality_of is an independent, weaker re-implementation.
findings.description: hop_locality_of returns `local` purely on `entry.get("dispatch_group") == "local"`. It ignores the provider-block fallback, the CLI exclusion and the endpoint-host check that hop_is_local applies. The locality recorded in the audit chain can therefore disagree with the locality the planner used to dispatch the hop.
findings.failure_mode: MODELINV hop_locality is wrong for block-level-local providers (records hosted) and would record `local` for a `kind: cli` model entry carrying dispatch_group: local if one slipped past load-time validation, so the audit field cannot be relied on to reconstruct where a prompt went.
findings.suggested_fix: Have hop_locality_of delegate to loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(hounfour, provider, model_id) (imported lazily like split_url already is) and delete the duplicate rule.

findings.cross_file_justification: create_ledger_entry now writes a third pricing_source value (`stale_catalog`) into the shared JSONL ledger. Only rollup.py was updated in this diff; cost-report.sh (named in this file's own comments as a ledger reader) and any other reader comparing pricing_source == "config" are not in the change set.
findings.description: A new enum value is introduced into a persisted ledger field. rollup.py was taught that `stale_catalog` is a priced row, but the diff does not touch cost-report.sh or other consumers that classify rows by `pricing_source == "config"`. Those readers will bucket stale-priced rows as unpriced/unknown even though cost_micro_usd and pricing_resolution are set.
findings.failure_mode: Cost reports and budget views undercount priced spend and overcount unpriced calls as soon as any catalog entry crosses the 90-day price_date window, with no error surfaced.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep every ledger reader (cost-report.sh, dashboards, bats tests) for `pricing_source` and treat `stale_catalog` as priced, or keep pricing_source="config" and record staleness in a separate additive field (e.g. `pricing_stale: true`) so existing readers need no change.
